ABOUT THE TOOL

Know what you’re measuring.

PadLab is an independent, free browser tool for observing gamepad inputs. It helps you investigate a controller’s behavior without installing a diagnostic application.

Our testing method

The tester reads currently exposed devices with the Gamepad API. The interface updates at approximately 30 frames per second while the page is visible. Button coverage records which pressed states were observed during the selected controller’s session. A three-second drift sample reports average and peak radial distance from center, as well as directional averages in the exported JSON.

What we do not measure

PadLab does not measure true input latency, USB polling frequency, electrical switch quality, microphone performance or battery health. It does not rewrite hardware calibration. Its visual deadzone never alters raw readings or your controller settings.

Compatibility and interpretation

Standard browser mappings enable the controller illustration and stick pairs. Unmapped devices retain numbered input feedback. Vibration is available only when a supported actuator is exposed. Results depend on the operating system, browser, controller firmware and connection.

Editorial approach

Our guides explain the tool’s actual behavior and link to technical references. No brand endorsements, device certifications or physical laboratory tests are implied. PadLab is not affiliated with Microsoft, Sony, Nintendo or other controller manufacturers.
